basis: Cerebellar degeneration defines SCA14. Frequent Achilles morphology annotations do not establish direct tendon damage; hypotonia and nystagmus are neurologic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: Achilles morphology is annotated in 30-79%, but direct tendon injury or functional impairment is not established.

basis: Bacterial infection targets circulating leukocytes; hepatocellular injury with elevated aminotransferases occurs in roughly 50-90% of common human anaplasmosis/ehrlichiosis cases.

decisions.hepatic: involved: direct hepatocellular injury occurs in roughly 50-90% of the common human infections represented by this umbrella.

basis: Developmental delay and sparse hair occur in 3/3; ventricular septal defect in 1/3 (~33%). Minor digit and tooth morphology does not establish functional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: brachydactyly and adducted thumb each occur in 1/3, but direct locomotor impairment is not established; short stature alone is insufficient.

basis: Inherited axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle wasting and foot deformities result from denervation rather than direct disease of muscle, bone or joints.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: neurogenic weakness, wasting and secondary deformities do not establish direct musculoskeletal damage by the disease process.

basis: Intellectual impairment, congenital cardiac defects/cardiomyopathy and thumb aplasia/hypoplasia define the phenotype; pigment changes alone do not establish skin damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: characteristic hypo/hyperpigmentation does not establish skin injury or loss of function.

basis: Constitutional polyploidy commonly causes CNS and limb malformations; congenital cardiac defects occur in roughly 30-50%, with variation by subtype and mosaicism.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiac malformations affect roughly 30-50% of constitutional polyploidy cases; frequency varies with subtype and mosaicism.

basis: GnRH deficiency defines the endocrine disorder. Anosmia is optional; subtype frequencies for olfactory, hearing and skeletal impairment are not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: olfactory dysfunction is optional, and neither the supplied HPO annotations nor subtype evidence establishes a frequency of at least 30%.

basis: Streptobacillary infection commonly presents as rat-bite fever; inflammatory polyarthritis occurs in about 50%. Transient rash does not establish skin damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: inflammatory polyarthritis occurs in about 50% of streptobacillary rat-bite fever cases and represents joint inflammation, beyond arthralgia alone.

basis: Immune granulomas affect lungs in ~90%; uveitis and liver dysfunction are HPO frequent (30-79%). Skin involvement and cytopenias omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: involved: decreased liver function is HPO frequent (30-79%), supporting functional injury from granulomatous involvement.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary granulomatous disease occurs in ~90%; the umbrella is defined by multisystem immune granulomas rather than a required pulmonary site.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: skin lesions are HPO frequent (30-79%), but pulmonary, ocular and hepatic functional injury take priority.

basis: Skeletal muscle channelopathy and ventricular arrhythmias define the syndrome. Frequent dental morphology abnormalities do not establish functional oral damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental crowding and unspecified dentition abnormalities lack established functional damage; oligodontia and retained primary teeth are occasional (5-29%).
